arguments.value: Robert F. Rossiter Jr. was born in 1956 in Camp Lejeune, North Carolina. He has served as a United States District Judge for the District of Nebraska since his nomination by President Barack Obama in 2015, confirmation by the Senate in 2016, and receipt of his commission later that year, and he served as chief judge from 2021 to 2026. Judge Rossiter earned his B.S. from Purdue University in 1978 and his J.D. from Creighton University School of Law in 1981. He began his legal career as a law clerk to Judges Albert G. Schatz and C. Arlen Beam of the U.S. District Court for the District of Nebraska, taught as an adjunct faculty member at Creighton University School of Law, and practiced privately in Omaha from 1983 to 2016.
